4.1  Setup Environments. We build long-input versions of GSM8K ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ) , MATH ( Hendrycks et al., 2021 ) , DROP ( Dua et al., 2019 ) , MBPP ( Austin et al., 2021 ) and HumanEval ( Chen et al., 2021 ) . A problem’s own unit (its statements, passage or
function specification) is placed among 30 to 90 units of other problems, so one
worker reading everything is not already as good as any team. A document holds
81, 91, 31, 61 and 61 units, and the test splits have 790, 220, 800, 333 and 131
problems (Appendix H ). These are our own constructions, not the standard benchmarks, so absolute accuracies are not comparable with published numbers on the originals; every system is evaluated on the same constructed inputs. Every system receives the same question text,
which includes the opening words of the target unit. The baselines also read the
whole document; the orchestrated team reaches it only through an evidence finder,
whose BM25 retriever the baselines lack, or a generalist that reads all of it. All
workers are Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ( Yang et al., 2024 ) served by vLLM ( Kwon et al., 2023 ) at temperature 1, following the protocol of MaAS ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) . Orchestration task. At each of at most five decisions (four on code)
the orchestrator calls one of eight roles (planner, evidence finder, analyst,
second answerer, calculator, checker, selector) or stops; code adds MaAS’s
test-and-repair operator. It observes an embedding of the task and a few state
flags, never a score. The reward is accuracy minus λ \lambda times tokens per 32,768 32{,}768 . We train with λ = 0.076 \lambda{=}0.076 , the protocol’s value (IAPO), and with λ = 1 \lambda{=}1 , which trades accuracy for tokens (IAPO-Lite). Our trajectories are
capped at 32,768 32{,}768 tokens; the baselines, which read the whole document, run
with 131,072 131{,}072 or 393,216 393{,}216 tokens. Training and certification. IAPO runs one round from the uniform
policy. It fits one bounded update for each step in Λ = { 0.25 , 0.5 , 1 } \Lambda{=}\{0.25,0.5,1\} on 6,400 6{,}400 proposal episodes ( 200 200 training problems, 32 32 repeats each), adds
three certified leaps (Appendix F.1 ), and certifies every candidate
with betting bounds at total level δ = 0.05 \delta{=}0.05 on 8,000 8{,}000 validation episodes
drawn from the remaining training problems. Test problems are never used for
fitting or selection. The certificate covers net return on the validation
distribution, so test accuracy is an empirical question. Search and training tokens
are excluded from the per-problem costs; one MBPP run uses about 1.7 × 10 8 1.7\times 10^{8} in total (Appendix I ). Each configuration is trained twice (three
times for MATH, IAPO), results are averaged over runs, and all rules were fixed
before the runs. Evaluation. Each test problem is run four times, and we report accuracy
and tokens per problem for one episode. Since the baselines spend more tokens, we
also evaluate at matched budget : a majority vote (on code, MaAS’s selector
over programs, with its tokens counted) over the most episodes whose tokens fit the
strongest baseline’s. The number of episodes never depends on accuracy. Differences
are paired by problem and called significant when z > 2 z>2 (Appendix I ). Baselines. We run fifteen published systems on the same executor and
splits, each as released, so none has a retriever. The single-agent group is CoT ( Wei et al., 2022 ) , ComplexCoT ( Fu et al., 2023 ) and self-consistency ( Wang et al., 2023 ) . The hand-crafted multi-agent group is MultiPersona ( Wang et al., 2024 ) , LLM-Debate ( Du et al., 2023 ) , LLM-Blender ( Jiang et al., 2023 ) , DyLAN ( Liu et al., 2023 ) , AgentVerse ( Chen et al., 2023 ) and MacNet ( Qian et al., 2025 ) . The automated group is
AutoAgents ( Chen et al., 2024 ) , GPTSwarm ( Zhuge et al., 2024 ) , ADAS ( Hu et al., 2025 ) , AFlow ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) , MAS-Zero ( Ke et al., 2025 ) and MaAS ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) . Not every system runs on every benchmark, and
Appendix H lists the setup of each.

4.4  What the Policies Deploy The deployed plans show where the interaction term pays (Appendix J ).
Test-and-repair helps only after a program exists, a pair of decisions. IAPO deploys
it in all four code runs; the first-order variant never proposes it, fills the slots
with a second programmer, and loses 17 17 points on MBPP and 7 7 on HumanEval at 3.1 3.1 and 1.8 1.8 times the tokens. On question answering and mathematics, all seven
IAPO runs follow the evidence finder with the analyst, usually with a checker and the
second answerer after it, while the first-order variant never calls the analyst and
reads the whole document with the second answerer instead. The analyst alone loses
points on every benchmark, so a first-order score never selects it, yet following the
evidence finder with the analyst gains (Appendix J ).

4.5  Controlled Tasks One probability q q is shared by N N decisions with frozen binary workers, and all 2 N 2^{N} trajectories are enumerated (Appendix G ).
Complementarity is the trap of Proposition E.7 , Redundancy has
substitutes, and Evidence threshold has N = 6 N{=}6 . The first-order score is zero for every step on Complementarity (oracle gain 0.148 0.148 ) and
overshoots on Redundancy ( 0.006 0.006 against 0.010 0.010 ), while the second-order score picks
the oracle step on both. On Evidence threshold the truncation bound exceeds the
second-order gain, so Z 2 Z_{2} alone deploys a gain of 0.087 0.087 , and adding Z IS Z_{\mathrm{IS}} restores 0.356 0.356 . Across 6,000 6{,}000 validation runs, no candidate with negative gain
was accepted.

Every declared plan is scored by the proposal statistic at its leap policy, the plan mixed with ε = 0.001 \varepsilon=0.001 of the reference, as the mean over the 6,400 6{,}400 proposal trajectories minus two standard errors. On question answering and mathematics the 50 top-ranked plans each run on 1,000 1{,}000 fresh validation draws and the three with the largest mean net return become the leaps; on code the three top-ranked plans become the leaps directly. The certificate never reads the screening draws. The expansion serves here as a proposal heuristic for distant plans, so the remainder bound does not apply to the leap ratios, while their certificates stay valid because they use paired draws of their own. Matched budget. The frozen deployed policy is rerun on the test split with a fresh salt and 10 to 200 repeats per problem. On answer tasks a vote takes the most common non-empty answer key over the first K K episodes, with ties to the earliest; on code the episodes split into groups of K K , each reduced to one program by MaAS’s HumanEval-template selector with its tokens added. K K is the largest count whose tokens per vote fit the strongest baseline’s tokens per episode, for every listed seed. The budgets are 28.6k (GSM8K), 53.8k (MATH), 57.1k (DROP) and 26.5k tokens (HumanEval); on MBPP it is 35.4k, below DyLAN’s 121.9k. Statistics.
